spot.html_text: The Cut rule can be stated like this: if from some premises (call them ⟦M⟧ ) we can prove the conclusion ⟦M⟧ , and if from ⟦M⟧ together with more premises (call them ⟦M⟧ ) we can prove ⟦M⟧ then we can prove the conclusion ⟦M⟧ from the premises ⟦M⟧ and ⟦M⟧ taken together. ⟦M⟧ Here, there is no restriction on the form of any of the particular judgements featuring in the rule. The particular premises and conclusions are completely general, so Cut is a structural rule.
